keyTakeaways.headline: GDB lands an RM877m logistics-hub contract in Shah Alam - its largest win this year - lifting the watchlist builder's outstanding order book to RM2.93 billion
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Two five-storey logistics hubs for Rochester Logistics Asset 2 extend GDB's pivot into high-spec industrial builds; the award re-rates its order book just as DC and logistics construction pipelines crowd in.

keyTakeaways.headline: IOI Properties' deleveraging programme lands in one day: IOIPG REIT priced at 96 sen (raising RM2.1b), a S$6b Singapore private fund being marketed and an SGX secondary listing targeted for early 2027
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The REIT alone cuts gearing toward 35% and anchors on IOI City Mall; the Singapore fund is the bigger lever - a 50% sale could raise close to RM10b - so watch pricing and cornerstone demand on both.

keyTakeaways.headline: Palm oil stockpiles are seen hitting a fresh record of 3.76m tonnes in October even as CRESS power contracting accelerates for data centres
keyTakeaways.soWhat: A fifth straight monthly production record keeps CPO prices under pressure into MPOB data next week; meanwhile TNB-IOI Corp's 500MW Bahau solar JV and Northern Solar's Johor DC LOAs show plantation and utility names monetising the DC power theme.

sectors.theme: Perak explores a 100MW-plus AI data centre; GPU server and PC supply contracts land for MM Computer and Theta Edge; Northern Solar says its Johor DC CRESS values are not yet final; TNB commits RM43b to grid modernisation

items.headline: Perak state development corp and Global Vision Lab explore AI data centre with planned capacity exceeding 100MW
items.detail: Perak State Development Corporation (PKNPk) and Global Vision Lab Sdn Bhd (GVL) have signed only a non-disclosure agreement and a letter of consent to exchange information and run preliminary assessments for an AI data centre in Perak, with planned power capacity exceeding 100MW. The facility targets AI computing, high-performance computing and GPU-based applications demand in Malaysia and the region. PKNPk coordinates state-level stakeholders while GVL leads development planning; full scope and capacity are still to be determined.
items.soWhat: Another state joins the DC land race beyond the established Cyberjaya-Johor axis, but with no NDA-stage commitment, land, power or water secured, this is intent rather than a project; the signal is that state agencies are now actively courting DC developers.
items.watchOut: NDA-stage only - no site, power purchase or anchor customer disclosed.

items.headline: MM Computer Systems bags RM51.58m order to supply GPU-accelerated servers to an unnamed Malaysian telco infrastructure and DC services provider
items.detail: MM Computer Systems Bhd secured a purchase order worth RM51.58 million through wholly-owned subsidiary Micro Technology Solution Sdn Bhd to supply GPU-accelerated servers supporting generative AI, large language model training and inference, deep learning and high-performance computing workloads. The customer is described only as a Malaysian telecommunications infrastructure and data centre services provider.
items.soWhat: A second AI-infrastructure hardware order in the domestic market within days (after Theta Edge) shows enterprise and carrier-grade AI capex is flowing to local system integrators, not only hyperscalers.

items.headline: Theta Edge wins RM33.01m contract as exclusive supplier of up to 5,742 laptops and desktops to Aceteam Networks under a device-as-a-service model
items.detail: Theta Edge Bhd's wholly-owned Theta Technologies Sdn Bhd will exclusively supply up to 5,742 new laptops and desktop computers to IT solutions firm Aceteam Networks Sdn Bhd under a device-as-a-service project covering provision and lifecycle management of the equipment. The five-year contract starts with first delivery and runs from completion of user acceptance testing; Aceteam operates in cybersecurity, cloud computing and data networking.
items.soWhat: Annuity-style device-as-a-service revenue improves earnings visibility for a smaller ICT name; watch margin on hardware-heavy deals against financing costs of the device fleet.

items.headline: Huawei Malaysia and CelcomDigi sign three-year workforce upskilling partnership covering AI, data analytics, 5G and cloud
items.detail: Huawei Technologies (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd and CelcomDigi Bhd entered a three-year memorandum of understanding to strengthen digital skills across the telco group's workforce, with Huawei providing access to advanced training, leadership programmes and industry-recognised certifications in AI, data analytics, 5G and cloud technologies, plus Huawei certifications at associate, professional and expert levels.
items.soWhat: Telco talent development is table stakes, but the Huawei channel into CelcomDigi's enterprise transformation keeps the vendor embedded in the group's AI ambitions; no commercial value disclosed.

items.headline: Northern Solar tells Bursa its two DC CRESS letters of award (89MWac and 100MWac solar plus BESS, both in Johor) have no finalised contract value yet
items.detail: Replying to a Bursa Malaysia query, Northern Solar Holdings Bhd clarified that the value of its two corporate renewable energy supply scheme projects - 89MWac and 100MWac of solar with battery energy storage, serving data centres in Johor with annual energy requirements of 233.9 million kWh and 262.8 million kWh - has yet to be finalised, with further announcements on execution of definitive agreements; the exact DC locations are confidential under the LOAs.
items.soWhat: Yesterday's headline capacity is real but commercially unpriced - revenue timing and margin for CRESS-linked solar EPCC stay uncertain until definitive agreements; treat LOA-stage DC-power wins across the sector with the same discount.
items.watchOut: LOA-stage only; contract value, tenure and tariff all undisclosed.

items.headline: TNB steps up grid modernisation with about RM43b of network investments under RP4 (2025-2027), including the 500kV National Grid Backbone
items.detail: Tenaga Nasional Bhd president and CEO Datuk Seri Shamsul Ahmad told a Singapore International Energy Week panel that TNB is investing ahead of demand, with about RM43 billion allocated for network investments under Regulatory Period 4 covering 2025 to 2027, supporting critical infrastructure including the 500-kilovolt National Grid Backbone and renewable energy integration. TNB serves approximately 11 million customers.
items.soWhat: Grid capex at this scale is the enabling layer for both DC load growth and CRESS connections; it frames a multi-year work pipeline for transmission contractors, cable makers and equipment vendors.

sectors.theme: GDB's RM877m Shah Alam logistics hub headlines a day of contract wins; flood mitigation gets a PM-level push; Pekat clears the SC for its Main Market move; ECRL revenue projections published

items.headline: GDB bags RM877m contract to demolish a factory and build two five-storey logistics hubs in Seksyen 15, Shah Alam; order book rises to RM2.93b
items.detail: GDB Holdings Bhd's wholly-owned Grand Dynamic Builders Sdn Bhd accepted a letter of award dated 30 October from Rochester Logistics Asset 2 Sdn Bhd on 2 November for main contract works: demolition of an existing factory and construction of two five-storey logistics hub buildings with integrated mezzanine offices and a dedicated three-storey cafeteria on PT 845, Jalan 15/23, Seksyen 15, Shah Alam, for RM877 million inclusive of 6% service tax. Back-to-back wins take GDB's outstanding order book to RM2.93 billion.
items.soWhat: Watchlist: this is GDB's largest single award this year and deepens its high-spec logistics/industrial niche at premium margins; client is an asset vehicle (Rochester Logistics Asset 2), so counterparty funding is the risk to track.
items.opportunity: Order-book cover now multi-year; logistics-hub demand from e-commerce and DC-adjacent supply chains keeps the tender pipeline active.
items.watchOut: Single-client concentration in one asset vehicle; verify Rochester Logistics' funding as works progress.

items.headline: ES Sunlogy wins two Kerjaya Prospek electrical subcontracts worth RM25.07m for the Pulau Andaman, Penang serviced-apartment project
items.detail: ES Sunlogy Bhd's wholly-owned Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd accepted two letters of acceptance from Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd: a RM19.87 million subcontract to supply and install electrical and extra-low voltage systems for two 46-storey, 1,080-unit serviced apartment towers in Bandar Tanjung Pinang (completion by 31 December 2029), and a RM5.2 million infrastructure works subcontract.
items.soWhat: Kerjaya Prospek's Penang mega-project is now flowing down to M&E subcontractors; for ES Sunlogy the award extends a customer relationship that dominates its order book - a double-edged concentration.

items.headline: PM Anwar orders Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects expedited after repeated flooding
items.detail: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered work on the Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects in Selangor to be expedited following repeated flooding in the area, Bernama reported.
items.soWhat: Accelerated flood-mitigation timelines pull forward civil-works spending; contractors with DID track records should watch for compressed tender schedules on these two schemes.

items.headline: Pekat Group gets SC approval to transfer to the Main Market, over five years after its ACE Market debut
items.detail: The Securities Commission Malaysia approved solar engineering firm Pekat Group Bhd's transfer of listing from the ACE Market to the Main Market on 3 November, noting compliance with the Bumiputera equity requirement. Pekat met the financial tests, including combined net profit of at least RM30 million over three financial years; it first announced the transfer plan in June.
items.soWhat: Main Market status widens the institutional investor base for a solar EPCC that is also assembling industrial land (yesterday's Nilai acquisition); read together, Pekat is positioning for larger CRESS-linked balance-sheet growth.

items.headline: ECRL passenger revenue projected at RM192m-RM204m a year for 2027-2029; cargo income seen tripling to RM214m by 2029, says Loke
items.detail: Transport Minister Anthony Loke said in a written parliamentary reply that East Coast Rail Link passenger revenue is forecast at RM192 million in 2027, RM198 million in 2028 and RM204 million in 2029, based on a 2025 consultant's study, while cargo revenue is projected to rise from RM68 million in 2027 to RM71 million in 2028 and then more than triple to RM214 million in 2029 - caveated as subject to actual operating performance.
items.soWhat: The first official revenue trajectory for the ECRL ahead of its January 2027 passenger launch sets a modest baseline: passenger income alone covers a fraction of operating costs, making the 2029 cargo inflection the number to watch for the project's economics and follow-on east-coast development.

sectors.theme: IOI Properties lines up a S$6b Singapore fund and an SGX listing; S P Setia adds a build-and-lease international school at Bandar Kinrara; Rehda Selangor presses for regulatory certainty

items.headline: IOI Properties to market a Singapore private real estate fund backed by S$6b of assets in coming months; targets SGX secondary listing in early 2027
items.detail: IOI Properties Group Bhd has started marketing a private real estate fund for its Singapore assets, worth S$6 billion (RM19.1 billion), to investors, CEO Datuk Lee Yeow Seng said; a 50% stake sale could raise nearly RM10 billion. The group is also targeting early 2027 for a secondary listing on the Singapore Exchange. Both moves, alongside the IOIPG REIT IPO, are part of efforts to deleverage after an acquisition spree.
items.soWhat: This is the largest of IOIPG's three deleveraging levers; pricing and investor appetite for Singapore commercial assets will signal whether regional capital still wants Malaysian-sponsored platforms.

items.headline: S P Setia signs build-and-lease deal with HELP for a 1,000-student international school at Bandar Kinrara, opening targeted for August 2029
items.detail: S P Setia Bhd subsidiary Perumahan Kinrara Bhd signed a build-and-lease agreement and a separate lease agreement with HELP Kinrara Sdn Bhd (under HELP Education Services) for a six-storey campus on Plot 5, a 2.01-acre site within a 16-acre commercial parcel planned as a transit-oriented development. Perumahan Kinrara builds; HELP fits out, obtains approvals and leases for an initial 15 years plus a five-year option. Indicative GFA is 176,085 sq ft with 55 classrooms; it would be the fourth HELP school, offering British curriculum to IGCSE.
items.soWhat: A long-lease education anchor de-risks the commercial plot of the former Kinrara cricket-field TOD and lifts surrounding residential value - a template other township developers are copying.

items.headline: Rehda Selangor calls for regulatory clarity, consistent policy and better agency coordination to support housing delivery
items.detail: Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Selangor chairman Datuk Edward Chong Sin Kiat told the Rehda Selangor Housing Convention 2026 that developers face rising development costs, changing market conditions and increasingly complex affordability, quality and sustainability expectations, and need certainty in requirements, decision-making and approval processes rather than guaranteed approvals.
items.soWhat: The state's largest developer body is publicly framing approval uncertainty - not demand - as the binding constraint; any state-level response on one-stop approvals would directly affect project timelines and holding costs.

sectors.theme: IOIPG REIT priced at 96 sen for a RM5.3b Main Market debut while retailers lobby MOF against foreign e-commerce

items.headline: IOIPG Malaysia REIT prices Main Market IPO at 96 sen per unit, raising RM2.1b for IOI Properties; RM5.3b market cap anchored on IOI City Mall
items.detail: IOIPG Malaysia Real Estate Investment Trust priced its Main Market IPO at 96 sen apiece, expected to raise RM2.1 billion for sponsor IOI Properties Group Bhd (the trust itself raises nothing), for a RM5.3 billion market capitalisation at listing. The initial portfolio is anchored by IOI City Mall in Putrajaya - Malaysia's largest shopping mall - alongside six hotels operating under Marriott International brands. The prospectus was issued 3 November with a 1-for-10 restricted offer to entitled IOIPG shareholders (up to 2.2 billion units; retail offering of 715.6 million units subject to clawback).
items.soWhat: Malaysia's largest retail asset finally lists as a pure-play; pricing at 96 sen tests yield appetite for mega-mall cash flows and gives the retail-REIT sector a new benchmark - watch the spread versus Sunway REIT and Pavilion REIT on debut.
items.opportunity: Cornerstone/institutional bookbuild response at 96 sen; restricted-offer take-up by IOIPG shareholders.
items.watchOut: Sponsor deleveraging, not fresh growth capital - the REIT starts life with a related-party tenant mix.

items.headline: MRCA warns of existential threat from foreign e-commerce in policy appeal to MOF, urging a fair-competition framework
items.detail: The Malaysia Retail Chain Association said it submitted a comprehensive set of policy recommendations to the Ministry of Finance urging a fair competition framework for foreign e-commerce platforms, citing severe market disparity as aggressively priced overseas goods undercut domestic retailers while platforms face less stringent tax and product-safety obligations. MRCA said it remains pro-business but insists any entity operating in Malaysia must adhere to national laws, tax obligations and product safety standards.
items.soWhat: Physical retail's lobby is escalating to the fiscal ministry ahead of Budget implementation; any levy or compliance tightening on cross-border e-commerce would flow straight into mall tenancy health and brick-and-mortar sales trajectories.

sectors.theme: October stockpiles seen at a fresh record on record output; IOI Corp joins TNB's 500MW Bahau CRESS solar JV; 50 more latex depots planned for 2027; Prosper keeps buying United Malacca at RM6.08

items.headline: Malaysian palm oil stockpiles likely swelled about 7% to a record 3.76m tonnes in October as output hit a record 2.2m tonnes - Bloomberg survey
items.detail: Malaysia's palm oil inventories likely expanded about 7% month-on-month to 3.76 million tonnes in October, surpassing September's record and running about 50% above the same month last year, according to the median of 11 estimates in a Bloomberg survey of plantation executives, traders and analysts. Crude palm oil output likely rose about 4% to a record 2.2 million tonnes, a fifth straight monthly increase, while exports surged; benchmark futures have retreated about 8% from their August peak and storage capacity is strained in parts of the country. Official MPOB data is due next week. (Bloomberg-sourced survey, attributed.)
items.soWhat: Record stocks into peak production keep CPO under pressure and squeeze upstream margins; the survey directionally frames MPOB risk for planters - integrated players with downstream or CRESS-style diversification (see pl-2) are better cushioned.
items.watchOut: Survey estimate, not official data; MPOB figures next week can move either way.

items.headline: TNB, IOI Corp and a 12-SME consortium sign JV for a 500MW Bahau, Negeri Sembilan solar project with 250MW/1,000MWh battery under CRESS
items.detail: Tenaga Nasional Bhd subsidiary TNB Renewables Sdn Bhd (TRe) signed a joint venture agreement with IOI Corporation Bhd's Luminous Aspect Sdn Bhd and a 12-SME consortium vehicle CSP 500MW Sdn Bhd to develop a 500MW solar power project in Bahau, Negeri Sembilan, including a 250MW/1,000MWh battery energy storage system, under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme. TRe holds 70% of Bahau Energy Ventures Sdn Bhd, Luminous Aspect 25% and CSP 500MW 5%; Tenaga will inject up to RM424.4 million, Luminous Aspect up to RM151.5 million and CSP up to RM30.3 million.
items.soWhat: IOI Corp is converting plantation landbank adjacency into CRESS renewables exposure at meaningful scale; for TNB this is another large CRESS JV that feeds the DC and green-power demand chain - and for the grid, BESS of 1,000MWh is among the largest committed domestically.

items.headline: Government plans about 50 more latex depots in 2027 to cut RM7b of annual latex imports; 137 sites identified, 30 operating
items.detail: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the government plans to develop about 50 latex depots next year to strengthen local rubber production and reduce reliance on latex imports, which currently reach RM7 billion a year. To date 137 latex depot locations have been identified nationwide with operations underway at 30, involving RISDA and the Malaysian Rubber Board.
items.soWhat: A domestic-latex buildout targets import substitution for the rubber-goods industry; execution history on smallholder collection schemes is mixed, so watch depot throughput rather than announcements.

items.headline: Prosper Trading buys another 20,800 United Malacca shares at RM6.08 in the open market under the conditional MGO
items.detail: In a dealings disclosure under the takeover rules, Prosper Trading Sdn Bhd acquired 13,000, 2,800 and 5,000 United Malacca Bhd shares from the open market on 2 November at RM6.08 each (excluding brokerage), while its conditional mandatory general offer at RM6.10 cash stands.
items.soWhat: The offeror buying at a two-sen discount to the offer price nudges its stake up cheaply and signals confidence the offer turns unconditional; each disclosure tightens the float minorities can sell into.
